issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for the getter of the ExcellenceLand.excellentEnough attribute: the UML/problem statement declares the attribute excellentEnough as a boolean (problem_statement.md lines 34-37) and requires public getters for all attributes, so the getter should return a boolean. In the solution (src/de/tum/in/ase/ExcellenceLand.java) the method isExcellentEnough() returns a String ("yes"/"no") instead of a boolean, which contradicts the specification and will cause tests or student expectations (boolean getter) to fail or be confusing.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the getter in ExcellenceLand to return a boolean to match the UML and problem requirements. For example: public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; } Update the solution (and template if it contains a placeholder) so the getter signature and return type match the boolean attribute declared in the UML/problem statement.
